patch_description:
The current program uses a population of 128, 16 elites, 6500 generations, a very small tail-support weight (0.0005), broad differential evolution only during the first 58% of the run, and no dedicated local polishing phase. Its long generation count increases runtime while the weak support score provides little guidance among configurations with nearly equal bottlenecks.

This revision uses a smaller, more efficient 112-member population over 3800 generations, 20 protected elites, stronger low-area support weighting (0.026), structured boundary/interior seeds, and a two-stage search. Early generations retain differential moves for basin discovery; later generations add active-constraint-aware offspring that preferentially perturb points occurring in the 8 smallest triangles. A final batched active-set local polish concentrates small moves on the current limiting triples while retaining occasional global sparse moves. This better targets the actual maximin constraints while reducing redundant evaluations and expected runtime.
